 Is DBS Group Holdings (SGX:D05) Still Undervalued On Excess Returns?
 Al Bentley Thu, November 19, 2026 at 9:19 AM PST 4 min read D05.SI +0.60% 
 DBS Group Holdings has delivered strong share price returns in recent years, which puts a sharper spotlight on whether the stock's current level is backed by the returns it earns on its capital. With the valuation lens now trained squarely on capital efficiency, investors are asking how much of that performance is already reflected in today's price. 
 Over the past 5 years, DBS Group Holdings has returned 205.4%, which makes the question of what its capital returns justify especially important for anyone considering the stock today. 
 The bank's role as a large, diversified lender with fee income and a sizeable deposit base can support a business model where returns on capital matter at least as much as headline growth, since every extra dollar invested needs to clear a high internal hurdle to create value. 
 Prefer to judge DBS Group Holdings on earnings? See why DBS Group Holdings's 17.3x P/E tells a different valuation story . 
 The stock's next move may depend on whether the returns DBS Group Holdings earns on its capital are strong enough to support the current share price. 
 If you want more ideas that put capital efficiency front and center, start your research with 206 high quality undervalued stocks . 
 Is DBS Group Holdings Still Cheap on Excess Returns? 
 The Excess Returns model starts by asking how effectively DBS Group Holdings turns its equity base into profits above its cost of capital. With an average return on equity of 17.27% and a cost of equity of SGD1.76 per share, the framework treats every extra dollar of equity as valuable only if it earns more than that charge. Book value sits at SGD24.67 per share, while stable book value is estimated at SGD25.95 per share, so the analysis leans on a bank that already carries a sizeable equity cushion. 
 Stable EPS of SGD4.48 per share and an excess return of SGD2.72 per share suggest DBS Group Holdings is modeled to earn more than its equity charge on a steady basis rather than needing aggressive expansion to justify the price. The dividend cross check, using a payout ratio of 57.94% and a capped long term dividend growth rate of 2.63%, points to an income stream that the model treats as continuing rather than one off. On that combined view, the Excess Returns projections put DBS Group Holdings' estimated intrinsic value meaningfully above the current share price of SGD67.34. Rather than stopping at a single output from a ratio or model, they unpack the future conditions that output rests on so you can watch, over time, whether those assumptions actually play out. Narratives sit on Simply Wall St's Community page and give you a structured way to think through what would need to happen next for DBS Group Holdings' current valuation to make sense. 
 Bulls see DBS Group Holdings as a long term Asia wealth and digital platform story, while bears focus on rate pressure and fee income risk. 
 Bull case: roughly fairly valued 
 This view comes from the analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St. It builds on shared forecasts rather than a single forecaster.
